newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU to negotiate ties with Korea nuclear group.
newsitem.headline: EU to negotiate ties with Korea nuclear group.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers told the European Commission on Tuesday to seek membership for the bloc in KEDO, the organisation for energy development on the Korean peninsula.
A Commission spokesman said the EU executive had been given a mandate to negotiate membership for EURATOM, the EU's nuclear energy body.
He said the mandate was to seek full participation for EURATOM and to give financial assistance to KEDO of a maximum of 15 million European currency units ($18 million) a year for five years.
KEDO, a consortium run by the United States, Japan and South Korea, is designed to ensure that North Korea's nuclear energy programme is steered towards peaceful means.

An EU source said Germany had had some concerns about the foreign ministers' decision, worrying about potential liability questions. Austria also said it had some concerns that its neutrality would be compromised.
